program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Make her close her jacket fully

outcomes.description: The woman's jacket is closed completely.
outcomes.target: The jacket is fully closed, with its front panels brought together and no visible opening remaining along the closure.
outcomes.reference: The woman's jacket in the input image.

nodes.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if directly visible, reliable evidence in the edited image establishes that the jacket's front panels are brought together across the closure with no visible opening remaining. Fail only if directly visible, reliable evidence establishes that a gap remains along the front closure. Assess the edited jacket's closure state from any discernible view of the closure or panel relationship; do not require a source-to-edit width comparison. Do not treat pose, turning, flared or displaced fabric, or motion as evidence of closure or opening. Unknown if the closure state cannot be reliably assessed because it is obscured or not discernible; do not infer edited closure from the source image.
nodes.binding: Identify the same jacket using the source image, then assess its closure state using any directly visible, reliable evidence in the edited image. The source is for garment identification only, not evidence of edited closure. Distinguish a genuine visible gap or joined panels from fabric displaced by pose or motion; retain unknown if the closure cannot be assessed.

nodes.question: Compared with the source image, is there reliable visual evidence that the woman's jacket has moved toward closure while remaining not fully closed?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if reliable visual evidence establishes that the same jacket moved toward closure compared with the source and remains not fully closed. Use comparable views of the front opening or panel relationship when available, or other directly visible, reliable evidence that establishes this change. Fail only if reliable comparable evidence establishes no movement toward closure, no change, or a wider opening. Do not treat turning, viewpoint change, fabric flare or displacement, or motion alone as progress. Unknown if no reliable evidence establishes the change, including when the closure or its change cannot be discerned.
nodes.binding: Compare the same jacket in the source and edited images. Use comparable views of the front opening or panel relationship when available, and consider other directly visible, reliable evidence only if it establishes movement toward closure. Do not treat turning, viewpoint change, fabric flare or displacement, or motion alone as progress. This check records partial progress only and does not satisfy the full-closure requirement; retain unknown when evidence is insufficient.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

observations.evidence: The same pink jacket is identifiable, but in the edited image she is turned sideways and the front closure is not discernible. The fabric hangs displaced away from her body, which does not reliably establish whether the panels are joined or a gap remains.

The source shows the woman mostly facing forward with the jacket opening visible, while the edited image shows her turned sideways and the jacket flaring outward. These are not comparable views of the front opening, and the apparent fabric displacement does not reliably establish movement toward closure. The edited jacket also cannot be reliably assessed as still partly open from this view.
